summary: A single purchase posts during the billing cycle, the statement closes with a balance well below the credit limit, and the cardholder pays the full statement balance before the due date. This exercises timely satisfaction of the minimum-payment obligation while also showing compliance with the credit-limit promise, so no late fee or over-limit fee should apply.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of this billing cycle, so the statement's new balance is determined entirely by the transactions in this cycle.
The credit limit is $1000.00, and the single purchase in this scenario keeps the account below that limit at all times.
The statement for this cycle closes on 2025-05-31 and sets a payment due date of 2025-06-25, which is at least 25 days later and consistent with the contract's purchase grace-period language.
The minimum payment for a $200.00 new balance is $15.00 under the contract formula, but the cardholder instead pays the full $200.00 by the due date.
The payment is made through an approved standard payment channel and is credited on the date received, with no returned payment and no posting delay.
No cash advances, foreign transactions, disputed charges, expedited payment fees, late-payment fee triggers, or over-credit-limit conditions occur in this scenario.
